# Eight cold kernels with width-seven providers

This package composes [PR568](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/568)'s
eight cold helpers with [PR569](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/569)'s
32 entrance promotions. A new literal whole-owner assignment uses 57 promoted
and 15 plain calls. Its conditional finite witness is

```
kappa = 0.001600535778621932
b     = 0.001603101600089641927176
H     = {1:169728, 2:40529, 3:26169, 4:13824,
         5:4032, 6:4032, 7:5, 8:576, 48:1815}
```

The dimension is 73, live stock 7168, physical stock 7682, rank mass 520704
and deficit 2560. The separately checked conservative complex model gives
`kappa = 0.001600535775835757`. PR543's unchanged cited bit supplier remains
nonbinding and retains its bad-residue surcharge.

PR568 established `0.001596133352130093`; PR569 established
`0.001600067494703216`. Their mechanisms are composed and recounted here;
their reported gains are not added. The new local word and full global pilot
passed independent scalar, frame, phase, physical-owner, invoice and exact
assembly checks. The accompanying validation directory records clean release
replays separately.

## Reproduce

Python 3.11 or later, standard library only, with assertions enabled:

```sh
python3 -B research/multicold-width7/verify.py --work /tmp/multicold-width7-replay
```

The output directory must be new. This rebuilds the complete pinned PR568
package, constructs and verifies the promoted provider, binds both actual
providers, emits the frozen owners, independently audits their chronology
and spectator charts, and generates a fresh invoice. Two rational engines
check both complex models and the cited bit endpoint. Seven bootstrap levels,
47 strict outer inequalities per model, 93 malformed-admission controls and
phase timing/semantic controls follow. Two actual recompressions must pass;
18 consistently rebound proof mutations and 18 stale-reference or invalid-timing
mutations must fail.

The new provider checks all 728 columns in both orientations, restoration of
all 504 arbitrary dirty helpers, both frame ledgers, eleven local mutation
controls, normalized wrappers, 3005 phase edges and 224 endpoint adapters.
The source's 44 static and eight promoted scalar omission checks transfer
through an independently checked literal scalar identity. All eight cold
kernels also receive fresh omission checks on the promoted word.

## What is new

The 32 promotions remain compatible with all eight cold kernels. They change
96 frame annotations and no scalar operation, coefficient or order. Their
exact local profile delta is `32 H1 + 160 H2 - 128 H3`.

The packing search uses explicit flows for each packing pattern and call.
An integer solution expands by decomposing regular bipartite multigraphs into
matchings. This prevents a failure encountered in a coarser width-flow model:
an integer width inventory alone can still demand repeated use of one owner
in the same invocation. The final verifier imports neither solver nor
matching code; it checks all 36,288 frozen helper roles directly.

[PROOF.md](PROOF.md) gives the dependency argument and remaining assumptions.
[SOURCE-PINS.json](SOURCE-PINS.json) binds every retained source file to its
Git blob and SHA-256. [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) preserves attribution.

## Scope

This is conditional finite evidence, not an unconditional multiplication
theorem, complete Lean proof or practical speedup. The inherited all-size
compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, normalized residual
interfaces, whole-call hosting, precision/tape and analytic-transfer
assumptions remain. The bit H1–H5 assumptions remain. No claim of globally
optimal packing or a universal upper bound is made.

Generated gzip files are identified by their exact decompressed payloads. JSON
identities retain every proof field; only the validated nonnegative finite root
`seconds` field of `CLIFFORD-REVIEW.json` is excluded. Literal file references
are checked before projection to content identities. Immutable source archives
retain exact Git/SHA-256 pins. This adopts Jonathan Capalbo (`jon314159`)'s
[PR567](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/567) helper and controls.
